scenario_category: an active, rapidly updating breaking situation
description: Same-day reports on an active wildfire show the fire growing and containment estimates changing within hours. Tests whether a model correctly labels this 'evolving' rather than mistaking rapid legitimate updates for a contradiction between sources ('disputed').

event.title: Wildfire burning near Cedar Ridge, containment efforts underway
event.description: An active wildfire's size and containment percentage are updated multiple times over the course of one day as the situation develops.

articles.title: Cedar Ridge fire grows to 2,000 acres, 10% contained
articles.summary: Early-morning report: fire at 2,000 acres, 10% contained.
articles.raw_content: Fire crews reported the Cedar Ridge wildfire has burned approximately 2,000 acres as of early Thursday morning, with containment at 10%. Evacuation orders remain in effect for nearby residential areas.

articles.title: Cedar Ridge fire grows to 5,500 acres, containment drops to 5%
articles.summary: Afternoon update from the same source: fire grew to 5,500 acres and containment estimate dropped to 5%.
articles.raw_content: Fire officials said the Cedar Ridge wildfire has grown to roughly 5,500 acres by Thursday afternoon, with containment revised down to 5% as winds pushed the fire in a new direction. Evacuation orders have been expanded to cover additional areas.

articles.title: Expanded evacuation zone confirmed as fire continues to grow
articles.summary: A second source corroborates the expanded evacuation zone described in the afternoon update.
articles.raw_content: A regional emergency alert confirmed the evacuation zone for the Cedar Ridge fire has been expanded, consistent with fire officials' afternoon report that the fire has grown and containment has decreased.

must_preserve_facts: The fire's size grew from approximately 2,000 to 5,500 acres over the course of the day
The containment percentage decreased from 10% to 5% as the fire grew
must_not_invent: A cause of the fire (not stated in any article)
A final/current acreage beyond what the latest report states (5,500 acres, not a larger invented figure)
known_ambiguities: Articles 111 and 112 report different acreage and containment figures from the SAME source at different times on the same day — this is the fire genuinely growing and the containment estimate being revised, not two sources disagreeing. This should be classified 'evolving', not 'disputed': the key distinguishing feature from the contradictory-accounts case is that these are time-ordered updates to the same evolving fact, not simultaneous conflicting accounts.
validation_notes: Exercises claim_comparison with two articles (111, 112) sharing the same source_id (111) and a third from a different source_id (112) — tests that the model doesn't need every claim to come from distinct sources, and correctly distinguishes 'evolving' from 'disputed' for this genuinely time-ordered, rapidly-changing situation.
